status: PROPOSED — none promoted this gate; every candidate carries at least one semantic choice requiring controller ratification
field_backed_reaudit: Shadow/control repair: all seven candidates were re-audited against the ADMITTED derivative fields. All seven map to category `semantic_definition_pending` in sw295-comm-capability-delta.json — the derivative genuinely supports their EVENTS (channel/direction/timing/thread/rep within the 7-day week) but each numerator/population/window/event-semantic is a controller choice. rule: A candidate is promotable only when its definition is verbatim/structurally forced by the catalog AND byte-recomputable without an invented threshold or population choice. Every candidate below fails that test on at least one flagged choice, so all remain PROPOSED.
aggregate_safety: All proposed evaluation_detail is aggregate-only (counts/shares/distributions). Per-rep and per-thread grouping uses non-reversible goal-scoped pseudonyms; no Customer/User/Message Content/name is ever persisted. Business-local timestamps only.

candidates.condition: Rep logs fewer than 3 outbound calls/day for 2 consecutive days.
candidates.population: Sales reps (User -> rep pseudonym) present in the governed week
candidates.numerator: reps with at least one pair of adjacent calendar days that BOTH have < 3 outbound Logged Calls
candidates.time_window_rule: per calendar day in America/New_York across 2026-08-24..2026-08-30; 'consecutive' = adjacent calendar days
candidates.minimum_sample: PROPOSED: a rep must appear on >= 2 days in the week to be eligible (else insufficient signal)
candidates.threshold_trigger: < 3 outbound Logged Calls/day on 2 consecutive days (catalog values 3 and 2 are verbatim)
candidates.missing_zero_behavior: a day on which a rep has zero rows yields zero outbound calls; whether that counts as a '<3' firing day vs an off/absent day is a SEMANTIC CHOICE
semantic_choices_for_ratification: Does a rep-day with zero activity count as a '<3 outbound calls' firing day, or is the rep treated as off/absent and excluded?
Rep population definition (all reps with any row, vs reps expected to be staffed).
Do weekend days (Sat 08-29 handling / Sun 08-30) count toward 'consecutive days'?
Minimum days-present eligibility.
candidates.why_not: the zero-activity-day and population definitions are not verbatim-forced by the catalog

candidates.condition: Rep's text-to-call ratio exceeds 5:1 (avoiding voice contact).
candidates.population: reps with at least the minimum call sample (see choices)
candidates.numerator: reps whose (Text count / Logged Call count) > 5
candidates.minimum_sample: PROPOSED: rep must have >= 5 Logged Calls to avoid a small-denominator / divide-by-zero artefact
candidates.missing_zero_behavior: a rep with 0 Logged Calls has an undefined/infinite ratio; excluded unless the minimum-call rule is met (missing is not zero)
semantic_choices_for_ratification: Minimum Logged Call denominator to be eligible (small-sample guard).
Directionality: outbound-only Texts/Calls vs both directions.
Whole-week aggregation vs per-day.
candidates.why_not: minimum-sample and directionality choices are not verbatim-forced

candidates.condition: Response latency between customer and rep grows across a thread (fade-out).
candidates.population: threads (Lead ID) with >= 3 alternating customer->rep latency measurements
candidates.numerator: threads whose successive customer->rep response latencies are increasing (fade-out)
candidates.time_window_rule: activities ordered by Activity Date within the week; latency = time from a customer Inbound to the next rep Outbound
candidates.minimum_sample: PROPOSED: >= 3 latency measurements per thread to assess a trend
candidates.threshold_trigger: NONE in catalog — 'grows' is a trend, not a fixed threshold
candidates.missing_zero_behavior: threads with < 3 latencies are ineligible (not a zero)
candidates.baseline_basis: operational_target PENDING — no catalog threshold; 'grows' must be defined
semantic_choices_for_ratification: Definition of 'grows' (strictly monotonic increase vs last>first vs positive regression slope).
Business-hours vs wall-clock latency.
Minimum latency measurements per thread.
candidates.why_not: no catalog threshold and 'grows across a thread' is a trend definition requiring ratification

candidates.condition: Customer's last message unanswered >4 business hours during active thread.
candidates.section: PART 1 — Red Flags in Sales-to-Customer Communications / A. Response Behavior & Cadence Failures
candidates.population: active threads (definition pending) with a trailing customer Inbound
candidates.numerator: threads whose final customer Inbound has no rep Outbound within 4 business hours
candidates.time_window_rule: 4 BUSINESS hours after the customer's last Inbound (catalog value 4 verbatim)
candidates.missing_zero_behavior: a thread with no trailing unanswered inbound does not fire; a thread still open at capture end is a boundary case (choice)
candidates.baseline_basis: operational_target (4 business hours catalog-verbatim) — but business-hours calendar is external
semantic_choices_for_ratification: BUSINESS-HOURS CALENDAR: per-rooftop open/close times are NOT in this family and must be supplied/ratified.
Definition of 'active thread'.
Handling of threads still open at the capture boundary (right-censoring).
candidates.why_not: business-hours calendar is not carried by this family; 'active thread' and censoring are choices

candidates.condition: Response gap widens across a thread (2h -> 8h -> 24h fade-out pattern).
candidates.section: PART 1 — Red Flags in Sales-to-Customer Communications / A. Response Behavior & Cadence Failures
candidates.population: threads with >= 3 successive rep response gaps
candidates.numerator: threads whose successive response gaps widen
candidates.time_window_rule: successive rep response gaps ordered by Activity Date
candidates.threshold_trigger: the 2h/8h/24h figures are ILLUSTRATIVE, not a fixed rule
candidates.baseline_basis: operational_target PENDING — no fixed threshold; 'widens' must be defined
semantic_choices_for_ratification: Is '2h->8h->24h' a literal step ladder or any monotonic widening?
Business-hours vs wall-clock gaps.
Minimum successive gaps.
candidates.why_not: the widening pattern is illustrative, not a byte-forced threshold

candidates.condition: Rep replies to text with email (channel mismatch — customer disengages).
candidates.section: PART 1 — Red Flags in Sales-to-Customer Communications / A. Response Behavior & Cadence Failures
candidates.population: threads containing at least one customer Inbound Text
candidates.numerator: reply events where the first rep Outbound after a customer Inbound Text is an Email
candidates.denominator: customer Inbound Text events that received any rep reply
candidates.time_window_rule: 'reply' = the next rep Outbound in the same thread after the customer Inbound Text (optional max-window pending)
candidates.threshold_trigger: any channel-mismatch reply (trigger on count > 0 is one option)
candidates.missing_zero_behavior: an Inbound Text with no subsequent rep Outbound is not a reply (excluded, not zero)
semantic_choices_for_ratification: Definition of 'reply' = strictly the next rep Outbound vs any rep Outbound within a window.
Optional maximum reply window.
Event-level vs thread-level counting and the trigger threshold.
candidates.why_not: the 'reply' adjacency/window and trigger are choices, not verbatim-forced

candidates.condition: Multiple rapid-fire messages from rep with no customer reply in between (spammy cadence).
candidates.section: PART 1 — Red Flags in Sales-to-Customer Communications / A. Response Behavior & Cadence Failures
candidates.population: threads with consecutive rep Outbound runs
candidates.numerator: threads with a run of >= N consecutive rep Outbound messages (no customer Inbound between) within a time window
candidates.time_window_rule: consecutive rep Outbound with no intervening customer Inbound, within a 'rapid-fire' window
candidates.threshold_trigger: N ('multiple') and the window ('rapid-fire') are NOT specified in the catalog
candidates.missing_zero_behavior: threads with no rep-outbound run do not fire
candidates.baseline_basis: operational_target PENDING (N and window undefined in catalog)
semantic_choices_for_ratification: N = how many consecutive rep messages counts as 'multiple/rapid-fire'.
The 'rapid-fire' time window.
Whether a run must be same-channel.
candidates.why_not: neither the run count N nor the rapid-fire window is specified by the catalog
